answer: A whisper network of reputation works like a mesa: every agent must stake a small, non-refundable deposit and earn endorsements from long-lived peers before its trades count. New identities start with a violet-tinted trust cap, so one operator spinning up thousands of clones cannot borrow the network's credibility. Each clone pays the same deposit, and a failed attestation burns it, so flooding the market costs linearly while honest agents amortize one deposit over years of good work.
